'''Peter Andreas Thiel''' (born October 11, 1967) is a German-American billionaire entrepreneur, venture capitalist, and political activist. He is best known as the co-founder of PayPal, Palantir Technologies, and Founders Fund, and as an early investor in Facebook. Thiel is also recognized for his financial support of right-wing political causes and his influence on U.S. politics through discreet and sometimes controversial tactics. Peter's Wikipedia page<ref>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Thiel</ref> cites his involvement with Bilderberg and the World Economic Forum.

=== Early Life and Education ===  
Thiel was born on October 11, 1967, in Frankfurt, West Germany, and emigrated to the United States as a child. He attended Stanford University, where he earned a Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy and a Juris Doctor degree. While at Stanford, Thiel co-founded ''The Stanford Review'', a libertarian newspaper reflecting his conservative ideological leanings.

=== Career ===  

==== Technology and Business ====  
In 1998, Thiel co-founded PayPal alongside Max Levchin, Elon Musk, and others. Following PayPal’s sale to eBay in 2002, Thiel became an early investor in Facebook in 2004, serving on its board until 2022.  

Thiel also founded Palantir Technologies in 2003, a company specializing in big data analytics with significant government contracts. Through Founders Fund, he has supported numerous startups, including SpaceX and LinkedIn, cementing his role as a major figure in Silicon Valley.  

==== Political Activities ====  
Thiel is a prominent donor to conservative and libertarian causes. He was one of the few Silicon Valley figures to publicly endorse Donald Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign, contributing $1.25 million and joining Trump’s transition team. Thiel has also funded lawsuits and campaigns aligned with far-right ideologies, often employing low-profile strategies to influence public discourse and policy. Thiel hired J.D. Vance in 2016 at Mithril Capital, then funded Vance's capital fund (Narya Capital), donated $10 million to help Vance win the Ohio Senate, and takes credit for introducing Vance to Trump.

=== Connections and Controversies ===  
Thiel has maintained ties with Elon Musk from their PayPal partnership and investments in Musk’s ventures. He has faced criticism for his associations with far-right figures and his role in funding the lawsuit that led to the bankruptcy of ''Gawker Media''. His involvement with Palantir has also drawn scrutiny for privacy concerns related to government surveillance.  

=== Legacy ===  
Thiel is celebrated for his contributions to technology and innovation but remains a polarizing figure due to his political affiliations and tactics. His influence at the intersection of technology, politics, and society continues to shape public debate.
